Question Text: Tom is a Servant leader of a complex software development project that is running using Agile development approach. Two developers are having difference in opinion about the technical approach of a user story. What needs to be done in this situation?
Selected Answer: Tom should assess the level of conflict and intervene appropriately
Correct Answer: Entire team should gather to discus the issue and produce a collective solution
Feedback: On an empowered agile team, it's up to the team members to resolve their technical disputes collectively. The scrum master, or the product owner is unlikely to have the knowledge required to make such technical decisions. So, among all options, option C is the best answer. Agile Practice Guide - Project Management Institute Inc., 2017, Page(s) – 41-43, 61.

Question Text: The project team is using Iteration burn-down chart to predict the remaining work in the current iteration backlog. Iteration Burn-down chart is an example of which of the following tools and techniques?
Selected Answer: Data Representation
Correct Answer: Data Analysis
Feedback: The burn-down chart is an example for data analysis tool that shows the total effort against the amount of work for each iteration. PMBOK Guide – Sixth Edition, Project Management Institute Inc., 2017, Page(s) – 226 & 687.

Question Text: A newly formed development team is started writing user stories after an understanding of the features and functions. The few examples of user stories are as follows: Users can make reservations so that they can travel Show room sizes so that they can see if it fits their need . Which one of the following problem would you like to fix in these user stories?
Selected Answer: The user stories are not explored from the user value point of view
Correct Answer: The user stories are not clarifying the specific users
Feedback: The user value is mentioned in these user stories. In first user story user wants to travel and in second user story users are visualizing value through their specific room size requirements. The estimates depend on size of user stories and question is not indicating that team has estimated these user stories as big in size. The user story is just a token of conversation and collaboration and writing acceptance criteria makes user stories testable. Above description eliminates following options: The user stories are not explored from the user value point of view The user stories are not small enough to estimate The user stories are not testable In these examples we can see development team is not mentioning the specific user roles – it is an important component of a user stories. Without specific intended user the identified value is vague and we are not aware who will benefit from it. If you are not aware about real user stories, then it is not right time to write user stories, first identify user roles like Student, Job seeker Employer for a Job Portal.

Question Text: A Release burndown chart is showing burn up, what could be the possible reason?
Selected Answer: The team is not delivering stories as per estimated velocity
Correct Answer: When new stories are added to release backlog.
Feedback: When additional work is added to a release , the team working with its normal velocity end up with more story points left at the end of iteration than they began working with.

Question Text: A permanent highly skilled staff hired for the project to avoid potential budget overruns. However, there is a risk of staff turnover during  the  course of the project, which may have an impact on the delivery. Which two actions should the project manager take to mitigate this risk? Choose two
Selected Answer: Introduce a recognition program to motivate and reward and reward resource performance. Increase the trained staff to create back up for resources.
Correct Answer: Introduce a recognition program to motivate and reward and reward resource performance. Increase the trained staff to create back up for resources.
Feedback: Two actions are: Increase the trained staff to create back up for resources and introduce a recognition program to motivate and reward resource performance.

Question Text: Which of the following is not an example of the four values of the Agile Manifesto?
Selected Answer: Working software is the primary measure of progress
Correct Answer: Working software is the primary measure of progress
Feedback: The options - A, C, D falls under four values of the Agile manifesto. Option B is an example for one of the twelve Agile principles behind the Agile manifesto. So, among all options, option B is the right answer. Agile Practice Guide - Project Management Institute Inc., 2017, Page(s) – 8,9.

Question Text: Tom is the newly appointed Project Manager of a software development project which has high degree of uncertainties and scope is not yet fully defined. Considering all the factors, he decides to adopt Agile development approach for running the project. Now, he has to come up with an initial cost estimate before the project work begins. What can be the best approach for the preparation of initial cost estimate as per the stated scenario?
Selected Answer: Using Analogous estimation technique to produce a high-level cost estimate
Correct Answer: Using light weight estimation methods to generate a high-level cost forecast.
Feedback: Projects with a high degree of uncertainty or if the scope is not fully defined may not benefit from detailed cost calculations because there are frequent changes. In an agile environment, lightweight estimates can be used to generate a high-level cost of project labor costs, which can be adjusted when changes are made. (PMBOK Guide) – Sixth Edition, Project Management Institute Inc., 2017, Page(s) – 234.

Question Text: Match the term with its corresponding description.

Todd is a project manager of a very large software product development project that needs to be executed from five different cities. Senior management has decided to run the project using an agile approach by following the philosophies of the scrum as much as possible. What framework is most suited as per the given situation?
Selected Answer: LeSS
Correct Answer: LeSS
Feedback: The situation in the question states about a very large project that needs to be executed using an agile approach by following the philosophies of the scrum. LeSS (Large Scale Scrum) is a framework that extends Scrum with scaling guidelines while preserving the original purposes of Scrum. It's most applicable for many teams (cross-functional) working together on one product. Agile Practice Guide, Project Management Institute Inc., 2017, Page(s) 20-23

Question Text: A team member shares with their functional manager some negative details about the performance of another team member that was discussed during the retrospective. The project manager finds out about this discussion. What two actions should the project manager take? Choose two.
Selected Answer: Meet with the entire team to review the ground rules about safe environments. Contact with the team member to explain what information can be shared outside the team.
Correct Answer: Meet with the entire team to review the ground rules about safe environments. Contact with the team member to explain what information can be shared outside the team.
Feedback: 1- Contact the team member to explain what information can be shared outside the team. 2- Meet with the entire team to review the ground rules about safe environments.

Question Text: At a walkthrough, a stakeholder, end user, and the development team identify significant new functionality required for the proposed solution to be effective. What is the next step?
Selected Answer: The new functionality should be added to the product backlog.
Correct Answer: The new functionality should be added to the product backlog.
Feedback: In agile, the development team commits to a group of user stories at the beginning of an iteration. Likewise, the product owner agrees not to disrupt the team during this timebox. For this reason, the best answer is that the new functionality should be added to the product backlog, to be estimated and prioritized later. Agile Practice Guide, Project Management Institute Inc., 2017, Page(s) 52-53

Question Text: Stakeholders want to understand what progress an agile team has made in their last iteration. What should stakeholders review to determine this information?
Selected Answer: The team's velocity chart
Correct Answer: The team's velocity chart
Feedback: The results of a spike would show team findings on a specific issue. A product backlog is a list of items to be developed for the project. In agile, 'fishbone analysis' is a genuine technique and one can 'slice' up user stories. However, combined 'fishbone slices' is a made-up term. Velocity charts show how much work the team has completed in each iteration. For each iteration, a velocity chart shows the amount of work completed . Agile Practice Guide, Project Management Institute Inc., 2017, Page(s) 64

Question Text: As an Agile Coach, what is the BEST way for you to handle a complex situation during a delivery?
Selected Answer: Allow the team to self-manage & adapt its process empirically
Correct Answer: Allow the team to self-manage & adapt its process empirically
Feedback: The Agile project manager should allow the team to self-manage & adjust its process as the team deems appropriate.

Question Text: Which of the following represents the purpose of Sprint review Meeting BEST?
Selected Answer: Team to present to the Product Owner and stakeholders functionality that is done
Correct Answer: Team to present to the Product Owner and stakeholders functionality that is done
Feedback: The purpose of the Sprint review is for the Team to present to the Product Owner and stakeholders functionality that is done.

Question Text: Members of the team post updates to a graph that shows the progression of features to being 'Done.' Examples of the stages of progress include Backlog, Design, Development, Testing and Done. What is the name of this graph?
Selected Answer: Product roadmap Graph
Correct Answer: Cumulative flow diagram
Feedback: A cumulative flow diagram depicts the progression of a set of features from start to finish. It's a Kanban way of monitoring work; Burndown chart does not reflect the stages of work.

Question Text: How does release plan help?
Selected Answer: Helps in Developing a WBS.
Correct Answer: Helps in understanding of the project's viability.
Feedback: Release plans helps in developing a better understanding of the project's viability.

Question Text: Which approach is BEST for estimating Agile Projects while doing the release planning?
Selected Answer: Bottom-up approach.
Correct Answer: Top down approach.
Feedback: A top down approach is used when estimating Agile Projects at the release level, as it is impossible to predict the work with any degree of certainty at the task level.

Question Text: During an iteration planning meeting, the team is estimating the size of the effort for each story by assigning each story to a shirt size of XS, S, M, L, XL or XXL. Which estimation method is being used?
Selected Answer: WBS estimating
Correct Answer: Affinity estimating
Feedback: The estimating scenario described here is affinity estimating. As we are grouping the stories in affinity for estimation purpose.

Question Text: The ongoing sprint for a software development project that is being executed by following Agile - Scrum development approach needs to be cancelled as the sprint goal has become obsolete due to a sudden change in law associated to IT security.Who will own the Product backlog?
Selected Answer: Product Owner.
Correct Answer: Product Owner.
Feedback: The product owner is responsible for maximizing the value of the product, and only he has authority to cancel the sprint, although he or she may do under the influence from key stakeholders, sponsor, project manager or any other stakeholders A sprint gets cancelled when sprint goal becomes obsolete due to sudden change associated to organizational policies, external environmental factors or due to any adverse situations impacting the project. Agile Practice Guide, Project Management Institute Inc., 2017, Page(s) 101

Question Text: The Scrum Master explains the three primary roles in Scrum to the newly hired team member. Which role is sometimes called 'the voice of the customer'?
Selected Answer: Product owner
Correct Answer: Product owner
Feedback: The product owner is defined as the "individual who serves as the voice of the customer, and who has the authority to make decision about the product. "The product owner is responsible for bridging the gaps between the customer, business stakeholders, and the development team. Agile Practice Guide, Project Management Institute Inc., 2017, Page(s) 41

Question Text: An agile practitioner is explaining the Agile Manifesto to some end users in advance of a new project. Which of the following would the agile practitioner say is preferred in an agile project?
Selected Answer: Collaborating with customers
Correct Answer: Collaborating with customers
Feedback: The Agile Manifesto lays out four values. Collaborating with the customer is preferable to contract negotiation. Likewise, individuals and interactions are valued more than processes and tools. Responding to change is more valued than following a plan, and working software is preferred over documentation. Agile Practice Guide, Project Management Institute Inc., 2017, Page(s) 8

Question Text: In a typical business complex and mid-sized agile project, what does the team attempt to develop every Sprint?
Selected Answer: A Potentially Releasable Product Increment
Correct Answer: A Potentially Releasable Product Increment
Feedback: The output of every Sprint is called a Potentially Releasable Product Increment. It is the sum of the Product Backlog Items completed during a Sprint. Delivering Potentially Releasable Product each Sprint is fundamental to the Scrum since in agile as work is divided into simple pieces, it can be finished in a short iteration. The product backlog is a living document that has anything and everything about project work. It is the ordered list of all the work presented in story form for a team Agile Practice Guide, Project Management Institute Inc., 2017, Page(s) 101

Question Text: The product owner of an agile project has the responsibility of grooming the product backlog. Grooming involves prioritizing and re-prioritizing user stories on a regular basis. As an agile best practice, which of the following criteria are most important for the owner to use when grooming the product backlog?
Selected Answer: Customer value and personas
Correct Answer: Customer value and risk
Feedback: The two most important criteria to consider when the product owner is grooming the product backlog is the value of the user story and the risk involved in the work required to complete the user story. High-value user stories are always considered high priority. High-risk user stories are typically prioritized so that the risk of project failure can be dealt with or determined early in the project before significant costs and resources have been devoted. Agile Practice Guide, Project Management Institute Inc., 2017, Page(s) 52-53

Question Text: A scrum team that has been working on an agile project, is arguing over the story points in the sprint meeting planning. The product owner is pushing the team to complete 170 story points of user stories in the next sprint whereas the average velocity of the development team is 150 story points per sprint. Who will make the final decision to fix the number of story points to be completed in a sprint?
Selected Answer: The development teams
Correct Answer: The development teams
Feedback: In the scrum, before making any commitment about the completion of user stories, development team discusses and then decides how many story points they can complete in the current sprint. It is the development team that is going to work on the product and know their capability and pace, therefore, the development team should make the final decision to fix the number of story points to be completed in a sprint.

Question Text: Which of the following is not a feature of an Agile team?
Selected Answer: Team members are 100% dedicated
Correct Answer: Each team member has a specialty
Feedback: An agile team is a cross-functional team. They are preferred to be a generalist. A cross-functional team is one with a variety of skills, abilities and experience, so that they can develop their scope (stories, features, "product backlog items", whatever) by themselves, without help from others.

Question Text: On the completion of the first three iterations, an agile team determined that 344 story points are required to complete the remaining project. The average team velocity in the first three iterations was 50 story points. What will be the number of iterations required for the team to complete the project?
Selected Answer: 7 Iterations
Correct Answer: 7 Iterations
Feedback: The velocity of the team is used to track the progress of the project and measured in terms of how many user stories it completes in one iteration. The average velocity of the team is measured based on its performance in the first few iterations .In this question, the average team velocity in the first three iterations was 50 story points. Now, 344 story points are left to complete the project. The number of iterations required to complete the project is calculated as the number of story points left divided by the average team velocity i.e. 344/50 in this case. It calculates at 6.88. In the case of iterations, we need to consider the whole number next to the result. Therefore, there is a need for 7 more iterations to complete the project.

Question Text: A team member is constantly spending on items that are not in the sprint backlog. As a Scrum Master what should you do?
Selected Answer: Talk to the member in person.
Correct Answer: Talk to the member in person.
Feedback: As a first step, Scrum Master should talk to the member in person to understand the situation better. Only if needed, the issue may be further discussed with the team.

Question Text: Florian is a stakeholder in STC company. He has recently learned that the team will use an agile framework in the current project. In a planning meeting, Florian tells the team members that they are not doing formal documentation in this project as they were doing in the previous projects. How will the team members reply to his statement?
Selected Answer: In agile, documentation is done for the clear work item only
Correct Answer: In agile Methodology, The documentation is kept barely sufficient to fulfill regulatory requirement
Feedback: Agile Manifesto Value number 2 states "Working software over comprehensive documentation". In agile, creating the formal documentation with a detailed description of everything is considered a wastage of time. It does not mean that documentation is not necessary at all. It is necessary but it should be kept barely sufficient to fulfill regulatory requirements in an agile environment. Although for some safety-critical products, some additional documentation and conformance checks are recommended.

Question Text: The velocity of an 8-member Agile team over the past few sprints has been 36, 32, 40, 46, 38 and 48 story points. In the next 2-week Sprint, there are two public holidays planned. How many points must the team plan for?
Selected Answer: 32 story points
Correct Answer: Whatever the team feel comfortable with
Feedback: The historical velocity is only a 'guideline' for future sprint planning – it is not a 'must' . The final decision on exactly how many points are picked up for the next Sprint rests with the team.

Question Text: One role of an agile practitioner is to promote the knowledge and execution of agile practices within an organization. Which of the following agile practitioners is responsible for the creation and maintenance of the product roadmap?
Selected Answer: Product owner
Correct Answer: Product owner
Feedback: The product owner is the voice of the customer and has the information and access required to define and prioritize development iterations, releases and ultimately a product roadmap. Once created the product owner is responsible for any changes required to the product roadmap and the individual releases that collectively form the roadmap. Agile Practice Guide, Project Management Institute Inc., 2017, Page(s) 41

Question Text: A team lead is currently demonstrating a potentially shippable product increment for project stakeholders. Which agile meeting is being conducted?
Selected Answer: Iteration review meeting
Correct Answer: Iteration review meeting
Feedback: At the end of each iteration, the project team demonstrates a potentially shippable product increment to project stakeholders during the iteration review meeting. These meetings may also be referred to as demonstrations or sprint reviews. Agile Practice Guide, Project Management Institute Inc., 2017, Page(s) 55

Question Text: At the sprint retrospective meeting, the team lead drew a fishbone diagram, wrote a problem at the head of the fish, and labeled the bones of the fish with categories. What should the team do next?
Selected Answer: Brainstorm factors within each category
Correct Answer: Brainstorm factors within each category
Feedback: After the problem is written at the head of the fish, and after the bones of the fish are labeled with categories, the next step is to brainstorm factors within each category. A Guide to the Project Management Body of Knowledge, (PMBOK® Guide) – Sixth Edition., 2017, Page(s), 293-294

Question Text: What is the most important reason why Product Owner needs to be present in Sprint Planning meeting?
Selected Answer: Decide team velocity based on historical performance
Correct Answer: Provide clarification on requirements
Feedback: Providing details on requirements is the most important reason PO needs to attend Sprint Planning meeting. Other three tasks need to be performed by the team.

Question Text: Team has finished release planning meeting and agreed on condition of satisfaction, priority of backlog items, team velocity, etc. There are some large features that were not estimated, however team decided to split them closer to development. Few sprints have passed, but team has not been able to update release plan due to time constraints. During Sprint Planning, team decides to split one large feature into 4 smaller stories based on operational boundaries. Unfortunately, there is not enough capacity in the current iteration, so team can include only 2 of the 4 stories in this sprint. When team demonstrates the product increment during the sprint review meeting, the PO refuses to accept these two user stories that the team had marked as Done. What could have potentially gone wrong?
Selected Answer: During Sprint planning meeting, condition of satisfaction or acceptance criteria may not have been discussed while splitting the user story.
Correct Answer: During Sprint planning meeting, condition of satisfaction or acceptance criteria may not have been discussed while splitting the user story.
Feedback: Conditions-of-satisfactions are continuously iterated, They are discussed and agreed upon, both at the start of release planning and iteration planning. In the question above the most likely scenario for PO not accepting the stories during Demo is that condition of the satisfaction of each of the user story derived by splitting feature, would have not been discussed. Since not all the user stories that comprised the feature were part of sprint it is even more important that definition of done is discussed for each story and not rely on definition of done for the feature which was agreed during release planning meeting. Team can split features based on operational boundaries, Release plan should be periodically revisited and revised however that is not the reason for problem, The definition of done is orthogonal to user acceptance criteria (functional acceptance) for a feature. It is a comprehensive checklist of necessary, value-added activities that assert the quality of a feature and not the functionality of that feature/story.

Question Text: How does an agile team go about developing a schedule?
Selected Answer: By estimating story points and making use of the team velocity
Correct Answer: By estimating story points and making use of the team velocity
Feedback: The team estimates story points and applies the team velocity (the rate at which the team completes story points), and derives a schedule.

Question Text: What role Product Owner plays in the sprint planning meeting?
Selected Answer: Product Owner grooms or maintains the Product Backlog and prioritized stories are used for sprint planning
Correct Answer: Product Owner grooms or maintains the Product Backlog and prioritized stories are used for sprint planning
Feedback: B is the best choice of the 4. The Product Owner creates and maintains the backlog for the product, therefore, the Product Owner directs the team activities by prioritize items in the backlog based on the anticipated value of each item.

Question Text: In evaluating an agile project, which of the following metrics would you use to compare effectiveness of two agile team / projects?
Selected Answer: Velocity
Correct Answer: Return on investment
Feedback: Agile recommends making people accountable for customer outcomes. Velocity is good for release planning but not for comparing two teams. You may think that Return on Investment goes beyond the scope of the team but it is not, the product owner and the team have to work on generating maximum value not high velocity.

Question Text: An agile team finished coding for the current iteration. Which of the following is a continuous process improvement ceremony that the team will now attend?
Selected Answer: Product demonstration meeting
Correct Answer: Iteration retrospective meeting
Feedback: The iteration retrospective meeting is a formal ceremony used in agile. This event is held at the end of each iteration where lessons learned during the iteration are reviewed, and specific plans of action are implemented during the next iteration to prevent these issues from occurring again on the project. Agile Practice Guide, Project Management Institute Inc., 2017, Page(s) 50-51

Question Text: While working on a hybrid project, an agile practitioner is responsible to perform the duties of both the project scrum master and provide project performance reports periodically to the senior management. The project sponsor suggests the agile practitioner that track the velocity of each team member individually instead of tracking the team velocity to monitor the progress of the project. What would the agile practitioner do as per agile best practices?
Selected Answer: Track and report only individual velocity to monitor the team performance
Correct Answer: Track and report only team velocity to monitor the team performance
Feedback: Agile best practices prefer to track and report the velocity of the team rather than the individual's velocity for monitoring the project. But some agile teams track the velocity of each team member individually in terms of completed story points or ideal days. This is not a good approach as it can cause behavioral issues in the team and can work against the success of the project team.

Question Text: Which two actions should a project manager consider while launching a new virtual team? (choose two)
Selected Answer: Verify if team member's own strengths and weaknesses as a virtual team leader to identify avoidable pitfalls
Correct Answer: Establish in the beginning, bow progress will be monitored and the means for communicating progress. Verify if team members are on more than one team and cannot devote enough time to this team.
Feedback: 1- Establish in the beginning, how progress will be monitored and the best means for communicating progress. 2- Verify if team members are on more than one team and cannot devote enough time to this team.

Question Text: You are an Agile practitioner working on an agile project using the Scrum framework. The primary purpose of a Sprint Review is for the team to?
Selected Answer: Demonstrate what was accomplished during the sprint.
Correct Answer: Demonstrate what was accomplished during the sprint.
Feedback: A Sprint Review is held at the end of the Sprint to inspect the Increment and adapt the Product Backlog if needed. During the Sprint Review, the Scrum Team and stakeholders collaborate about what was done in the Sprint. Based on that and any changes to the Product Backlog during the Sprint, attendees collaborate on the next things that could be done to optimize value.

Question Text: An agile team is working on a project for which the user stories have not been tested sufficiently. What could be the reason behind it?
Selected Answer: Incomplete definition of done
Correct Answer: Incomplete definition of done
Feedback: "Definition of the done" involves the tasks needed for the completion of the user story as well as testing of the specific functionalities. Code reviews, the different type of testing's and other criteria that the team thinks are needed to deliver a good quality product should be included in the "definition of done" of a user story. It provides a checklist of the tasks against which the team checks if a user story is complete or not.

Question Text: You have been appointed as the Servant Leader for your company's latest software development project running in agile framework. Which of the following defines your role?
Selected Answer: Your main role is to ensure the processes and help project team to remove impediments.
Correct Answer: Your main role is to ensure the processes and help project team to remove impediments.
Feedback: The Scrum Master ensures the process is successful and not the project.

Question Text: Based on the velocity determined after completing several iterations, agile team members assume that they will be unable to meet the release deadline. What should the team do?
Selected Answer: Slice user stories so that the team can increase velocity
Correct Answer: Meet with the product owner to re-prioritize the backlog
Feedback: Typically, on agile projects, the cost and the schedule are fixed, while the scope is flexible. Meeting with the product owner to discuss the scope reduction, or in other words, to re-prioritize the backlog, is the best option among the answer choices provided. Ultimately, it is up for the product owner to decide what to do based on input from the team. Agile Practice Guide, Project Management Institute Inc., 2017, Page(s) 52-53 , 91

Question Text: During a retrospective, the members of the agile team mention that the agile coach's actions during the last iteration did not align with agile best practices. To which of the following did the team most likely refer?
Selected Answer: The agile coach assigned user stories to individual team members
Correct Answer: The agile coach assigned user stories to individual team members
Feedback: Agile encourages self-directing and self-organizing teams, where the team members decide who will perform the work. The team members choose their work tasks for the next iteration. Agile teams thrive with servant leadership. In agile, the team members pull their work from an iteration backlog. The coach does not assign work to the development team. Agile Practice Guide, Project Management Institute Inc., 2017, Page(s) 33-39

Question Text: Which statement is true about the Sprint Burndown chart?
Selected Answer: It helps team assess how much work is remaining to be done, measured in story points
Correct Answer: It helps team assess how much work is remaining to be done, measured in ideal hours
Feedback: Sprint Burndown chart is based on tasks pending for the current Spring and depicts remaining work estimated in ideal hours. Release Burndown chart on the other hand plots story points remaining to be done at the release level.

Question Text: Assuming same team capacity, how would doubling the work in progress (WIP) affect Cycle Time?
Selected Answer: Doubling the work in progress (WIP) would double the Cycle Time
Correct Answer: Doubling the work in progress (WIP) would double the Cycle Time
Feedback: Per Little's Law, given same team capacity (and throughput), Cycle Time is directly proportional to total work in progress.

Question Text: Team with Product Owner have started sprint planning meeting for Sprint #3. Release duration is 4 months with 5 sprints. PO presents sprint goals and team is seeking clarification for one of the use stories. PO provides required explanation however she also mentions that for her to approve the user story in demo she need to have these three functionalities done and demonstrated in right way. Team has some doubts and discusses further with PO. After the discussion PO agrees to need of only two features to be demonstrated by team for her to approve the story. What team is doing in this scenario?
Selected Answer: Team is discussing and helping to define condition of satisfaction for sprint with product Owner
Correct Answer: Team is discussing and helping to define condition of satisfaction for sprint with product Owner
Feedback: User story is a short description of feature required and by who, User story is further discussed by team with PO to understand details of what functionalities are expected to be able to complete user story , there are called as condition of satisfaction.

Question Text: An agile team is in the process of adopting XP practices and is keen to have a co-located customer. But the customer team being in a different continent, customer co-location is not really an option. What is the next reasonable option for the long term?
Selected Answer: Use collaboration tools with the customer to reduce miscommunication and rework.
Correct Answer: Use collaboration tools with the customer to reduce miscommunication and rework.
Feedback: Though recommended for XP teams, customer co-location is not a must-have requirement. If not possible due to logistic reasons, the next best long-term option is to use collaboration tools to facilitate transparency, and reduce miscommunication and rework.

Question Text: An agile project to develop software for a new inventory control system is in the initiation stage. Which of the following would most likely be included in the project charter?
Selected Answer: The Project vision or purpose
Correct Answer: The Project vision or purpose
Feedback: Every project needs a project charter, so the project team knows why this project matters, where the team is headed and what the project objective is. At a minimum, for an agile project, the team needs the project vision or purpose and a clear set of working agreements. Agile Practice Guide, Project Management Institute Inc., 2017, Page(s) 49-50

Question Text: You are a scrum master, handing a team working on an agile project. The product owner could not take part in the recent sprint planning meeting due to his other responsibilities. A team member escalates in the daily standup meeting that he needs clarification for a user story, but not able to contact the product owner to get feedback. What will you do in this situation as a scrum manager?
Selected Answer: Contact the product owner on behalf of the team member
Correct Answer: Contact the product owner on behalf of the team member
Feedback: Agile Manifesto Principle emphasizes that the developers and business stakeholders should work together daily throughout the life of the project. In agile practices, it is the product owner who takes the decisions regarding the product.

Question Text: The newly-organized agile project team is creating the schedule management plan, they documented time-boxed periods for releases, waves, and iterations for the project. What is the project team trying to achieve by documenting time-boxed periods for each iteration?
Selected Answer: Minimize scope creep
Correct Answer: Minimize scope creep
Feedback: For this situation, the agile project team is *documenting time-boxing to help in minimizing scope creep* as it forces the teams to process essential features first, then other features when time permits. Options B, C, and D are not relevant for the given scenario. PMBOK Guide – Sixth Edition, Project Management Institute Inc., 2017, Page(s) – 182.

Question Text: In a Scrum project, the term "done" is BEST described when a deliverable is:
Selected Answer: Complete as mutually agreed by the team & product owner
Correct Answer: Complete as mutually agreed by the team & product owner
Feedback: The use of "done" is indicative of the deliverable having been completed as mutually agreed to by the team & product stakeholders. The team keeps detail checklist which explains or list outs the done criteria.

Question Text: You are working as an agile practitioner and in the middle of the project the developing team lead came to you mentioned that he is interested in the operation manager position which was published internally in the company. What would be your action?
Selected Answer: Discuss it first with the product owner to see the impact on the project
Correct Answer: Support him to grow as he has the talent
Feedback: You would need to support him in growing then an agreement can be done with the team lead that he can support the project with educating one of the team members with taking his role. Other answers would demotivate him if you think he really would fit in the new role and he has the skills for it.

Question Text: In Agile methods, project planning may take place at 3 levels, such as visioning, release planning, and iteration planning. These 3 levels are examples of what?
Selected Answer: Refactoring
Correct Answer: Progressive elaboration
Feedback: Progressing from vision to release to iteration is an example of progressively elaborating on the plans for a project, from highlevel to low level.

Question Text: Your Company has hired a Lean consultant. The consultant is having discussion with the team about flow of work, team roles, processes, documentation, and lesson learned. What should be the top priority of lean consultant during this review?
Selected Answer: Identify and eliminate waste
Correct Answer: Identify and eliminate waste
Feedback: at the core of Lean, is the principle of eliminating waste. So the first focus of the consultant should be identifying and eliminating waste,

Question Text: Senior management calls the Product Owner to understand the detailed project status. What should the Product Owner do?
Selected Answer: Redirect management to the electronic tool that hosts release plan, Scrum board, and different project metrics.
Correct Answer: Redirect management to the electronic tool that hosts release plan, Scrum board, and different project metrics.
Feedback: The scrum board and electronic tool are important information radiators that serve as a quick project status for all stakeholders – the team, customer, and the rest of the organization. This could be used for basic project reporting. Only in case of additional management reporting requirements, a meeting or document may be required.

Question Text: To compensate for the loss of productivity due to inefficient communication in a distributed team environment, management created a team of 14 members. But, the team is performing far below expectations. What should the management do next?
Selected Answer: Co-locate all the team members
Correct Answer: Split the team into two teams
Feedback: 14 members is a very high number even for a co-located team. The first thing the management should try is to split the team into two teams, favouring co-location as much as possible.

Question Text: Two teams are working on different projects. Team A averages 20 points per iteration and team B averages 35. What can be said about the performance of the two teams?
Selected Answer: No comparison about performance can be made based solely on these figures
Correct Answer: No comparison about performance can be made based solely on these figures
Feedback: Since story points are used to 'estimate' and are not standardized, what comparison can you make between teams? One should not compare the performance of the two agile teams based on individual team velocity. The size of a story point is unique for each team. Thus, it is impossible to say which team is more productive based on their velocity. Agile Practice Guide, Project Management Institute Inc., 2017, Page(s) 66

Question Text: In the mid of a software development project, a project stakeholder requests the scrum master for adding a new feature that will increase the project cost and schedule. What should the Scrum Master do next?
Selected Answer: Set up a meeting between the project stakeholder and the product owner.
Correct Answer: Set up a meeting between the project stakeholder and the product owner.
Feedback: The Product owner is responsible for guiding the direction of the product that includes features and functionality, cost, schedule. The product owner is the person who is ultimately accountable for the end product that is built. The product owner works with customers and the teams to define and maintain the product direction. Agile Practice Guide, Project Management Institute Inc., 2017, Page(s) 40,41

Question Text: How should an agile practitioner respond when asked what type of planning corresponds to the technique of applying incremental delivery cycles to perform the work on an agile project?
Selected Answer: Rolling wave planning
Correct Answer: Adaptive planning
Feedback: Option C & D are terms not associated with Agile Project Management. Rolling wave planning is a form of progressive elaboration that focuses more on the near term plans and rolls into the long term as more information becomes available about the project requirements. Adaptive planning describes the technique of applying incremental delivery cycles to plan and perform the work on an agile project. Agile Practice Guide, Project Management Institute Inc., 2017, Page(s) 17-25

Question Text: During project execution, one of the key project team members needs to take an unexpected leave of absence. The project is ahead of schedule and under budget. Which two actions should the project manager take initially to resolve this problem? (choose two)
Selected Answer: Check the project's responsibility assignment matrix (RAM) to determine which activities will be affected. Check the risk register for a prepared response to resource being suddenly unavailable
Correct Answer: Check the project's responsibility assignment matrix (RAM) to determine which activities will be affected. Check the risk register for a prepared response to resource being suddenly unavailable
Feedback: 1- Check the risk register for a prepared response to a resource being suddenly unavailable. 2- Check the project's responsibility assignment matrix (RAM) to determine which activities will be affected.

Question Text: To increase agile knowledge, traditional project managers of a company have been paired with scrum masters to observe them lead their teams. One observation is that many project decisions are the responsibility of the project team and the scrum master is more facilitative than authoritative. In fact, the scrum masters seem more focused on ensuring that the team can focus on the work, have a shared vision, and determine how they will accomplish their work. What leadership approach have the scrum masters adopted?
Selected Answer: Servant leadership
Correct Answer: Servant leadership
Feedback: Servant leadership is the practice of leading through service to the team, by focusing on understanding and addressing the needs and development of the team members in order to enable the highest possible team performance. Agile Practice Guide, Project Management Institute Inc., 2017, Page(s) 17-25

Question Text: Agile principles encourage the use of particularly decision models. Which of the following is FALSE about participative decision making?
Selected Answer: In Participatory decision making everyone votes on the decision, and no decision can be implemented without a unanimous vote
Correct Answer: In Participatory decision making everyone votes on the decision, and no decision can be implemented without a unanimous vote
Feedback: in consensus decision making everyone votes on the decision, and no decision can be implemented without a unanimous vote. In participatory decision making, team members participate in the decision process, and the decision is made by a preponderance of the vote.

Question Text: How is risk managed in Agile?
Selected Answer: Risk is monitored & audited on an ongoing basis throughout each iteration & exposed during iteration planning, execution, review & retrospective
Correct Answer: Risk is monitored & audited on an ongoing basis throughout each iteration & exposed during iteration planning, execution, review & retrospective
Feedback: Risk is assessed during iteration planning & audited at retrospective meetings, while burndown charts & stand-up meetings expose any ongoing risks to the team.

Question Text: During the project, the product owner knows from the sponsor that a major component, which is already 20 percent completed, is not needed anymore for the users. The component was part of the approved scope. As a product owner what should you do next?
Selected Answer: Directly tell the team to stop developing it
Correct Answer: Discuss for a formal approval from the sponsor to discontinue developing it
Feedback: This component was approved to be in the product backlog and moved to a sprint where team is already working on it. It is better to have formal approval from the sponsor to cancel or discontinue working with this component.

Question Text: Team is finding hard to understand one of the acceptance tests written on story cards. What is the next BEST step?
Selected Answer: Discuss within the team
Correct Answer: Discuss with the customer
Feedback: Customer is part of the development team, and the team should feel free to discuss such issues with customers.

Question Text: You are the Scrum master and having a conversation with one business stakeholders Joy, Joy asked, how do business people interact with development team? For instance, business people only understand the business benefit of possible feature where the development team speaks about technology, what brings both of them on the same page? You said:
Selected Answer: The product owner is responsible to break the business requirements into engineering tasks which team can understand
Correct Answer: The Product Backlog is understood by Business as well as by the team
Feedback: Product Backlog is a Common Denominator between Product Owner and Team both understand it well, the team makes engineering tasks based on the Product Backlog on their own.

Question Text: A set of related user stories that may be combined together and treated as a single entity for either estimating or release planning is referred to as:
Selected Answer: Epic
Correct Answer: Theme
Feedback: It's a definition of theme.

Question Text: You are the scrum master and you notice that over the last 6 iterations, the number escaped defects has gradually increased. Yet the numbers are not alarming, but the trend is not favourable. What should you do first?
Selected Answer: Do an analysis of the development process
Correct Answer: Bring the discovery to the attention of the team
Feedback: All 4 options are not bad, and the Scrum Master may find it useful to take steps. However, the question asks what should be done first. The first responsibility is to share this information with the team and let the team own it.

Question Text: An agile practitioner needs to track the work completed by the team over time. How might the agile practitioner accomplish this task?
Selected Answer: Calculate the team's velocity
Correct Answer: Calculate the team's velocity
Feedback: Velocity is perhaps the most common metric and is used to determine the team's capacity over time. It is often used to compare actual completed work to estimated work. Agile Practice Guide, Project Management Institute Inc., 2017, Page(s) 61,64

Question Text: An agile team is demonstrating a recently developed product. Who determines when a product is complete?
Selected Answer: The development team
Correct Answer: The product owner
Feedback: The team defines the definition of done (DoD), but it is the product owner who accepts the delivered stories as being complete. The DoD is a clear and concise list of requirements that the user story must satisfy for the team to call it complete. The DoD must apply to all items in the backlog. Acceptance criteria, on the other hand, are uniquely defined for each item in the backlog and are used by the product owner to declare a story complete. Agile Practice Guide, Project Management Institute Inc., 2017, Page(s) 41

Question Text: During the iteration planning meeting, you come across a story whose development does not fit into an iteration. What is the BEST thing to do next?
Selected Answer: Split the story into smaller stories.
Correct Answer: Split the story into smaller stories.
Feedback: One should split a story into multiple smaller stories that can be accommodated into an iteration length.

Question Text: Exploratory tester use all the following tools EXCEPT?
Selected Answer: Test Cases
Correct Answer: Test Cases
Feedback: Exploratory testers uses the following four tools to explore the software. Tool #1: Charters Before beginning an exploratory session, a tester should have some idea of what to explore in the system and what kinds of things to look for. This charter helps keep the session focused. Tool #2: Observation Tool #3: Notetaking Exploratory testers keep a notepad beside them as they explore and periodically take notes on the actions they take. Tool #4: Heuristics A heuristic is a guide: a technique that aids in your explorations.

Question Text: Susanne is the product manager for one of the critical go to market product for Foremost enterprise. IT team developing the product has chosen KANBAN methodology to deliver the product. Susanne is invited to daily standup meetings and she is quite pleased with the progress so far and quality of discussions during the daily standup meetings. She has observed that just after the daily standup meetings are complete some small groups of 2-3 team members go to different room and discuss some issue. She asks one such group on what they were discussing and she was told it was mostly some architectural or process related issues. Susanne wonders why they are not been discussed in daily standup meetings. She approached the Project Manager of the team. What should project manager do?
Selected Answer: PM should tell Susanne that she should not worry about such meetings as After Meetings are common practice in KANBAN to generate improvement ideas
Correct Answer: PM should tell Susanne that she should not worry about such meetings as After Meetings are common practice in KANBAN to generate improvement ideas
Feedback: Such meeting which happens after daily standups are After Meeting consists of huddles of small groups of 2 or 3 people. This emerged as spontaneous behaviour as folks want to discuss something on their mind and may often result in improvement ideas.

Question Text: It is the Sprint Planning meeting for 3rd sprint of an 8-sprint release. One user story is too large and team decides to split it into smaller stories. There are several ways team could split user stories EXCEPT:
Selected Answer: Splitting the user stories based on the data that will be supported or based on data variations
Correct Answer: Splitting user stories based on relative weightage of risk and business value for each of the smaller stories.
Feedback: Relative weightage of risk and business value is used to prioritize user stories, but is not recommended to split a user story into smaller stories.

Question Text: Team was working on iteration 3 and during the testing, tester identified bugs in a story completed in iteration no 1, what should be the team's response?
Selected Answer: This bug is treated the same way as a user story. The fixing will prioritize into a subsequent iteration in the same way that any other user story would be.
Correct Answer: This bug is treated the same way as a user story. The fixing will prioritize into a subsequent iteration in the same way that any other user story would be.
Feedback: The bug found in finished iteration stories need to be treated as a story for prioritization in subsequent iterations, they do not get scheduled into the next iteration automatically.

Question Text: You are project Manager and have been participating in initial discussion with product Managers, business and architect team to reach an agreement on work in progress limit for your team. After analyzing the nature of work and other parameters you have proposed a Work in progress limit of 50 however Business stakeholders want WIP in progress limit to be increased to 75 as there is need to faster time to market. As a Project manager what are the factors you should consider before deciding on WIP limits.
Selected Answer: WIP limits are mostly influenced by Queue size and needs to be determined during the course of the project as more information is available to team
Correct Answer: WIP limits is influenced by Queue and buffer size , both of these needs to be empirically adjusted as required as the project progresses
Feedback: WIP limits is influenced by Queue and buffer size , both of these needs to be empirically adjusted as required as the project progresses.

Question Text: If the product owner said that the last sprint failed to deliver value to the project What should the scrum master mention at the next retrospective?
Selected Answer: Issues that arose
Correct Answer: Issues that arose
Feedback: Issues which come and happened during that sprint needs to be discussed and present on the table during the retrospective meeting.

Question Text: While working on a sprint an agile team notice that an important task on the sprint backlog will take more time than it was estimated. What should the agile team do?
Selected Answer: Continue working in the task until it is completed
Correct Answer: Stop working on the task and plan it for next iteration
Feedback: Stop working on the task and plan it for next iteration) some times some tasks need more time than originally estimated and the task is important maybe it needs to be done as one box, Stop working on it and keep focusing on it for next iteration.With stopping it they may finish the sprint early and start directly once the new iteration start Note that :If it [means the sprint then answer is 3] if it means the story then as we know sprint is a time-boxed framework.

Question Text: You are the Product Owner and you see an updated burndown chart depicting the progress of the current iteration. The team is on day 10 of 30-day iteration. The card depicts the planned progress as a diagonal line in yellow. Actuals are updated each day, forming a green line. On day 10, the green line below the yellow line. What does this communicate to stakeholders?
Selected Answer: New Tasks are getting added in the Sprint backlog which is hampering the progress
Correct Answer: This iteration is going well- the team is ahead of the plan
Feedback: The green line indicates the amount of ideal hours within which work has been completed. On day 10, the team is further along than planned, so the team has burned down the work faster than expected. Option D could be right but we should not jump to the conclusion as iteration is not yet over and we do not know whether the planned velocity was similar as that of the previous iteration.

Question Text: How do you BEST describe the primary role of Agile Leader?
Selected Answer: Manage teams without having to manage their tasks.
Correct Answer: Manage teams without having to manage their tasks.
Feedback: Agile leaders is cast in the role of managing teams by articulating project goals , objectives , vision etc. but leaving the teams to manage their own tasks.

Question Text: What trend does the top of the bar indicate in a release burndown bar chart?
Selected Answer: Work to be completed
Correct Answer: Work completed
Feedback: A release burndown bar chart uses bars to indicate the amount of work in the release. The top of the bar is lowered any time work is completed. This shows the velocity of the team.

Question Text: Who writes the User Stories?
Selected Answer: Developer
Correct Answer: Customer
Feedback: Customer is accountable for writing user stories, in many cases they are supported by proxies like business analysts but in principle they remain accountable for writing user stories.

Question Text: There are 5 levels of planning that are common to agile projects. If we list them from high-level to low-level planning, which of the following represents the correct sequence?
Selected Answer: Product vision, product roadmap, release plan, iteration plan, daily plan
Correct Answer: Product vision, product roadmap, release plan, iteration plan, daily plan
Feedback: B has the correct planning levels named and in the proper order.

Question Text: The project sponsor from the customer's side doesn't like most of what she sees in the product demo just before the first release of the product. And now the whole release could be in jeopardy. What do you think could possibly be the root cause of this situation?
Selected Answer: The Product Owner lacks the necessary experience to capture requirements in an effective manner or failed to communicate them to the team.
Correct Answer: The project sponsor was either not invited or failed to attend previous demo sessions that were conducted at the end of individual Sprints.
Feedback: If the project sponsor doesn't like most of what she sees, she is looking at the product probably for the first time. Faster feedback cycle with the customer is one of the key reasons why various Agile methods recommend developing the product in iterations.

Question Text: Agile has a lot of methodologies,frameworks and practices. (Drag and drop the items from Left to right )
Product Owner wants to include an urgent story into the current Sprint – on day 3 of a 2-week Sprint. How should the development team respond to this request?
Selected Answer: Take the change in but only as an exception, and request the Product Owner to take a roughly same-size story out of the Sprint
Correct Answer: Take the change in but only as an exception, and request the Product Owner to take a roughly same-size story out of the Sprint
Feedback: While the team may take in urgent changes into the current Sprint, under extreme circumstances, it should make sure the Sprint scope matches with the team capacity.

Question Text: In a Scrum team, who is responsible for the success or failure of the project?
Selected Answer: Development Team
Correct Answer: The entire Scrum team
Feedback: The responsibility for the success of the project is shared by the entire team.

Question Text: A team member has been coming late to the daily scrum for past several days. What should the Scrum Master do?
Selected Answer: Talk to the member to figure if he needs support.
Correct Answer: Talk to the member to figure if he needs support.
Feedback: As a first intervention, the Scrum Master should try to understand the root cause of such erring behaviour.

Question Text: Why do we write acceptance tests?
Selected Answer: Tests are used to fill in the details of a user story, it captures the assumption made by the customer while writing the user stories
Correct Answer: Tests are used to fill in the details of a user story, it captures the assumption made by the customer while writing the user stories
Feedback: Test notes captures assumptions made by the customer. Acceptance tests also provide basic criteria to determine if a story is fully implemented.

Question Text: The team wants to know how the product will be used, or what features will prove more popular. Of the following, what technique can help the most?
Selected Answer: Create personas
Correct Answer: Create personas
Feedback: Creating personas are the best choice for the scenario. The personas are like a fictional character or made up which represents your customer target segment.

Question Text: Which of the following statement is true about risk identification in agile teams?
Selected Answer: Risks gets identified in Daily stand-ups, iteration planning meetings, release planning meetings, demos, reviews, and retrospective meetings
Correct Answer: Risks gets identified in Daily stand-ups, iteration planning meetings, release planning meetings, demos, reviews, and retrospective meetings
Feedback: In agile we do organic risk management and risk can be identified in any of the planning meeting, no special meeting for just identifying risks.

Question Text: One of your stakeholders is interested in knowing how well agile team is doing in reducing the risks iteration by iteration, which of the following information radiator can help the most?
Selected Answer: Risk Burn Down Chart Solution
Correct Answer: Risk Burn Down Chart Solution
Feedback: The risk burn down chart displays how the cumulative risk exposure is reduced as the project is progressing though iterations.

Question Text: Who comes up with the definition of done for a feature?
Selected Answer: The quality-control specialist
Correct Answer: The team
Feedback: The team defines what done means. Typically it includes designed, coded, tested, and accepted by the Product Owner. Even though many stakeholders are included, yet it is the team that defines done. Lot of time we think it should be Product Owner or Customer, Customer / Product owner does defines the acceptance criteria for the user story but since the definition of done is more focused towards the engineering activities, it is defined by Team, and acceptance by Customer is usually part of definition of Done.

Question Text: A vice president of product management company taken the role of Product Owner for a business critical product. He is ideally suited to ensure product vision better, but he is struggling to spend enough time with the team. He is thinking to have a proxy for the lower level detailing of requirements. Who makes the best User Proxies?
Selected Answer: Salespersons
Correct Answer: Someone from the development team
Feedback: In Agile we don't need managers, we need leaders. When Product Owner is busy, then the first approach should be identifying the way to get realistic workload, and so that can work with their teams. It may not always be possible. A person from the development team who aware of technology world as well as the domain of the software. An analyst who puts effort into interacting with actual users is often an excellent user proxy.

Question Text: While transitioning from Waterfall to Agile, a team of 25 decides to create two development teams and one testing team, where the output of current development iterations is tested in the next testing iteration. This practice is likely to increase the following types of wastes EXCEPT:
Selected Answer: Delays
Correct Answer: Defects
Feedback: The number of defects are dependent on quality of development, and not when the testing actually takes place.

Question Text: In Scrum, how does developing product over multiple time-boxed sprints help in managing requirements:
Selected Answer: Developing a product over several iterations is a pre-condition for empirical process control.
Correct Answer: It helps balance the need for certainty vs. the benefits of adaptability.
Feedback: Developing a product over several iterations helps balance the need for certainty (within a sprint) vs. the benefits of adaptability (from one sprint to the next).

Question Text: Joy met with Sally so that he could describe in detail the change the customer wanted to make into a key feature of the product. While Joy talked about the technical specifications, Sally made eye contact with Joy. When Joy felt that all the details had been covered, Sally asked if she could repeat back her understanding to make sure it was complete and clear. In this scenario, sally is applying what technique?
Selected Answer: Active listening
Correct Answer: Active listening
Feedback: Active listening is the best description of what has been done. She made an eye contact and reviewed to confirm understanding by starting back to the other person what she listened carefully.

Question Text: Agile earned value management is most appropriately applied at which level?
Selected Answer: Wave
Correct Answer: Iteration
Feedback: Tracking and reporting of costs and accomplished story points is most appropriately applied at each iteration or sprint in a release. The Budget is prepared at release level, so you get a budget for release and you monitor the budget at the end of iteration.

Question Text: A Lean team employed a technique to analyse the flow of information and materials through system to identify value adding and non value adding activities. This technique is called:
Selected Answer: Pareto Lean paring
Correct Answer: Value stream mapping
Feedback: The question describes value stream mapping, used to better understand and streamline processes.

Question Text: You are a project manager for SubZero Delights, a company that offers extraordinary experiences to travelers. Your latest project involves the development of a smartphone app that automatically picks up a customer's GPS coordinates to provide tailored resources and recommendations. While documenting the resource management plan, you decide to incorporate a RACI. What does RACI stand for? (Select four.)
Selected Answer: Responsible Accountable Consult Inform
Correct Answer: Responsible Accountable Consult Inform
Feedback: RACI is a type of responsibility assignment matrix that captures resources assigned and how they are associated with the work of the project. RACI stands for responsible, accountable, consult, inform.

Question Text: You are a scrum master of scrum team. The new team member has just joined the team and has a very little experience in the domain you are working in. How should you manage him?
Selected Answer: Give him specific tasks so he can get started
Correct Answer: Spend time in modelling expected behaviour
Feedback: As a scrum master you do have a role to coach people, and when people join in the team your role comes into picture to explain what is expected out of him.

Question Text: A Development teams' velocity is around 40 story points, and they are accepting 5, 8, 13point stories in an iteration. The team is taking high priority items needed by the business and also Product Owner regularly involved during development. But still, the team is feeling urgency pressure and as a result consistently missing out one or two user stories in the iterations. As an Agile Practitioner, what would you like to suggest?
Selected Answer: Split large user stories in small user stories.
Correct Answer: Split large user stories in small user stories.
Feedback: The size of user stories looks like big especially for 8, 13 when the velocity is 40 points for an iteration. When stories are large, we need to split them to reduce complexity by looking into various possible small and valuable independent pieces within them. Large stories take more time compared to small one. The question is nothing indicating that team is poor in capacity planning, and they need training. When stories are big, then product backlog needs grooming for the splitting of user stories, but we have already more specific option: Splitting big user stories in small one and becomes best.

Question Text: Reducing the number of items in the team's immediate focus results in?
Selected Answer: Kanban task boards
Correct Answer: WIP Limits and increases productivity and quality
Feedback: It's a core focus of Kanban. Reduced Work In Progress is very effective at increasing the productivity and quality of the team's work.

Question Text: Team A is delivering 800 SP, and Team B is delivering 30 SP. Team B is going through some external interruptions after adding few resources. As an Agile Practioner, how would you define team A and team B?
Selected Answer: Adding resources in between of Sprint is not allowed, and it may impact the velocity of team B compared to team A
Correct Answer: Can't say anything about who is doing better, although Team B could increase their velocity by avoiding interruptions
Feedback: Each team has its definition of velocity, which cannot be comparable from other teams. Yes, adding resources in between slow-downs the velocity but still, Team A can not be compared with team B using velocity.

Question Text: Budget & schedule should be considered as conditions of satisfaction for which phase of planning?
Selected Answer: Product planning
Correct Answer: Release planning
Feedback: Budget & schedule are the two measures used for determining product success & should occur at the release planning phase.

Question Text: What style of leadership should agile leader adapt?
Selected Answer: Collaborative leadership
Correct Answer: Adaptive leadership
Feedback: Agile welcomes changing requirements as an opportunity to refine the product or the work performed to deliver more value and competitive advantage to the customer so agile leaders must be adaptive.

Question Text: Your team consists of a programmer, a designer, and a tester and you are asked to provide an estimate for a user story in terms of ideal days. What is the BEST approach for providing this estimate?
Selected Answer: This scenario is not suited for estimating in Ideal Days
Correct Answer: Provide a single estimate for the user story
Feedback: In estimating a user story in terms of Ideal Days, one should associate a single estimate with each user story, and this helps in deriving cross functional behaviour.

Question Text: Which of the following is an example of Avoid risk response category?
Selected Answer: Development of this feature is outsourced to other team
Correct Answer: This feature gets dropped from the product backlog because of the risk associated with it.
Feedback: Avoid talks about removing or avoiding the cause of risk, so here by dropping a feature we are avoiding the risk.

Question Text: Which could be the best possible approach for Splitting Epic?
Selected Answer: Disaggregation can be done along the lines to create, edit, and delete.
Correct Answer: Disaggregation can be done along the lines to create, edit, and delete.
Feedback: Since user stories focus on giving value to the user or purchaser , splitting stories based on the technical line will not give value to the user, if we split based on functions like create / edit / delete, each story gives value to the user.

Question Text: A development team is fully aware of their decisions, and consequences too. The whole development team have goals to achieve but are not directed how to achieve them. They are free to manage their work and can enhance their skills contineously. How would you describe this team?
Selected Answer: The team is empowered to develop own methods of working together
Correct Answer: The team is empowered to develop own methods of working together
Feedback: A self-organizing team is defined as: A group of motivated individuals, who work together toward a goal, have the ability and authority to take decisions and readily adapt to changing demands One of the Agile principles is that the best architectures, requirements, and designs emerge from self-organizing teams.

Question Text: Your team is in a good place; your velocity is gaining momentum with each new Sprint, and then suddenly your star developer turns in his resignation. Which one of the following practice will support the team best?
Selected Answer: The team member must be willing to share knowledge openly
Correct Answer: The team member must be willing to share knowledge openly
Feedback: Agile team is self-organizing. The sharing of knowledge among team members is important to success, as we look for collective code ownership. The team is not reliant on a PM / Scrum Master to make assignments.

Question Text: The team meets for the sprint planning meeting. Regarding the product backlog, what is the correct expectation of the team?
Selected Answer: The team expects to work with the Product Owner during the sprint planning meeting to help rank and prioritize the product backlog
Correct Answer: The team expects prioritized product backlog to work on from the product owner
Feedback: It is expected that The Product Owner carries out value-based prioritization PRIOR to the sprint planning meeting. The team (not the Product Owner or Scrum Master) commits to how many features or backlog items to team can produce in the next iteration or Sprint.

Question Text: In creating the team space, what feature provides the most effective method of communication?
Selected Answer: Desk positioning, creating a team space which promotes face-to-face interaction
Correct Answer: Desk positioning, creating a team space which promotes face-to-face interaction
Feedback: Face-to-face communications is the most effective; the majority of face-to-face conversation content is nonverbal.

Question Text: Which role is responsible to prepare the release plan?
Selected Answer: The Product Owner
Correct Answer: The Product Owner
Feedback: It's a role of a product owner.

Question Text: You are the scrum master of an underperforming and burnt-out agile team. How can you best improve the team's performance?
Selected Answer: Increase the number of daily stand-up meetings
Correct Answer: Take the team to lunch
Feedback: Sometimes simple solutions is the most effective in Agile. If a team is burnt out, a simple Solution: may be to take them to lunch to help boost morale. Other solutions are focused on more monitoring which will not be constructive.

Question Text: As per XP methodology , When XP teams perform significant analysis, design, coding and testing?
Selected Answer: Every day.
Correct Answer: Every day.
Feedback: XP teams perform significant analysis, design, testing, and coding every day.

Question Text: In a sprint planning meeting, who is responsible for selecting the number of items for the sprint from the product Backlog?
Selected Answer: Development Team.
Correct Answer: Development Team.
Feedback: The number of items selected from the Product Backlog for the Sprint is solely up to the development team. Only the development team can assess what it can accomplish over the upcoming Sprint. Product owner is responsible for the prioritization/rank of user stories according to business value.

Question Text: Your company implements a requirement that teams create highly detailed documentation as part of the company-wide software development lifecycle. What is the correct response?
Selected Answer: Use negotiation techniques to help the organization become more agile
Correct Answer: Select a process for the team that delivers the highly detailed documentation without sacrificing delivery of customer value
Feedback: When your company has a requirement for all teams, you need to comply with it. That's why agile teams tailor their process based on how the wider organization functions. But they still make sure that they are focused first and foremost on delivering value to the customer.

Question Text: You are an agile practitioner. Several members of your team have expressed concern that the project is not progressing as well as they would like. What is the best course of action?
Selected Answer: Post a burn-down chart in a highly visible part of the team space
Correct Answer: Post a burn-down chart in a highly visible part of the team space
Feedback: An agile practitioner should practice visualization of important project information by maintaining information radiators that are highly visible. It's important that they show the team's real progress, and a burn-down chart is a great way to do that.

Question Text: Your project sponsor wants to know if the product you're building will be ready to demo at a trade show.What do you tell him?
Selected Answer: We'll get your top-priority functionality done by then.
Correct Answer: We'll get your top-priority functionality done by then.
Feedback: In this case, you need to know that agile teams will typically fix time and cost and allow scope to vary, as reflectedin the agile triangle.When balancing constraints, the agile approachis to get the highest-priority product functionality done by the customer's deadline.

Question Text: As Scrum Master, you assess that the competitive market has shifted and the product the team is building is no longer viable.What should you do?
Selected Answer: Ask the product owner if the viability of the project has changed.
Correct Answer: Ask the product owner if the viability of the project has changed.
Feedback: The ScrumMaster can't terminate theproject because he don't make those kinds o fdecisions. he also wouldn't direct the product owner what to do when. The only person on a Scrum team who has the information needed to assess the viability of the project is theproduct owner.So the correct answeris "ask theproduct ownerifthe viability ofthe projecthas changed."

Question Text: You are leading a team with an average velocity of 65 points per iteration.Another team of the same size in your organizationis working on aproject with similar complexity. The other team's velocityis averaging 90 points per month.Your team should:
Selected Answer: Perform affinity estimating to check their estimates, since something is off
Correct Answer: Ignore the difference
Feedback: Velocity is team-specific and unique to that team.In other words, a story point for one team probably wouldn't have the same value as a story point for another team.Therefore,it is not appropriate to compare velocities between teams. The best choice would be to ignore the difference.

Question Text: Influences in the projects (Drag and drop the items from Left to right)

Your team is averaging 40 story pointsper two-week iteration.they have 200 points' worth of functionality left in the user story backlog.How many weeks can we expect it will take until development is completed?
Feedback: The average 40 points per iteration, we should get through a 200-point backlog in 5 iterations (200 / 40= 5).Each iterationis 2 weeks long, so 5 iterations is equivalent to 10 weeks (5x2=10). The key to answeringthis question correctly is noticing that the question asked for the number of weeks,not the number of iterations.

Question Text: As per agile estimating tools and techniques So, Affinity estimating allows a team to:
Selected Answer: Check that stories within the same functional areas are of similar proportion.
Correct Answer: Confirm that stories that have been estimated as the same size are of equivalent magnitude.
Feedback: Affinity estimation involves a process of triangulation to confirm that stories estimated to be the same size are of equivalent magnitude.

Question Text: You have been assigned a New Project that is large, complex and uncertain. As a Project Manager, you will be using agile project management. Which of the following will you select while creating your team?
Selected Answer: None of the above
Correct Answer: None of the above
