Feedback: As per Agile methodology, it is best to work with small teams staffed by talented and experienced people and increase the number only when required.

Question Text: After the end of the fourth sprint, the agile team members reported that they were unable to complete all user stories to be delivered in the sprint since the product owner pushed too many story points for the last sprint. As a result, the team had to work overtime and eventually got burned out. The product owner wants to hold the team accountable for the sprint failure. What is the best course of action for the team in this situation?
Selected Answer: Not accept responsibility for the failure and hold the product owner accountable for pushing too many story points into the last sprint
Correct Answer: Accept the responsibility for the failure and hold retrospective to see how to improve the process for the next sprint
Feedback: Maintaining a constant pace indefinitely is one of the Agile Manifesto principles. The team should have planned work properly and accepted only the number of story points that they felt they could complete based on the velocity determined in the previous three sprints Agile Practice Guide, Project Management Institute Inc., 2017, Page(s) 50-51

Question Text: A team needs to perform various activities during Sprint Planning meeting. Which of the following activities should ideally be completed before Sprint Planning starts?
Selected Answer: Prioritize product Backlog items
Correct Answer: Prioritize product Backlog items
Feedback: A prioritized product backlog is an essential input for the Sprint Planning meeting. Other tasks are part of the Sprint Planning meeting.

Question Text: How should the team handle non-functional activities that are part of Definition of Done (DoD) but the Product Owner does not care much about?
Selected Answer: Try to convince Product Owner to add stories for non-functional activities in the product backlog
Correct Answer: Add estimates of all activities, taking into account the time spent in non-functional activities
Feedback: Non-functional activities like frequent integration, code review, test automation, etc. help the team manage risk and improve the quality of the product. The effort spent on such non-functional activities must be taken into consideration while estimating functional work items (features).

Question Text: During Daily Scrum meeting, a junior developer (A) shares that he is stuck on an important task. A senior developer (B) who has worked on a similar item in the past offers to help. As an Agile Practitioner, what step should you take?
Selected Answer: Request developer A and developer B to work on this task in pair-programming mode
Correct Answer: Request them to discuss the problem right after the Daily Scrum
Feedback: Daily Scrum is a good platform to raise impediments and identify who could possibly help, though the solution discussions must be kept short. 'Right after the Daily Scrum' is a good time to discuss the details of possible solution options.

Question Text: A developer has just learnt a better way of developing a feature the team just finished. He shared the details with the Scrum Master to show the possibility of improving the performance by a factor of two or more. How should the Scrum Master try to utilize this learning?
Selected Answer: Ask the Product Owner to add a technical story to refactor the feature just completed and prioritize for a future iteration.
Correct Answer: Share the details with team and discuss what to do about it.
Feedback: In an Agile project environment, development team is the best judge on technical decisions. Scrum Master should facilitate in creating an environment where knowledge is shared openly and decisions are takes with team consensus.

Question Text: Due to the organizational constraints, some of the agile team members are in different parts of the country, while other team members are co-located in the same building of the organization. Which of the following agile technique would establish better communication among the team members?
Selected Answer: Setting up a war room with the video conferencing capability
Correct Answer: Setting up a war room with the video conferencing capability
Feedback: Virtual co-location is an environment in which distributed teams take help of digital tools to imitate the physical colocation. The goal of virtual colocation is to get as much close as possible to get a feel of face to face communication.

Question Text: An agile practitioner is planning to share the project status with stakeholders. What approach should the agile practitioner take?
Selected Answer: Use highly visible posters, displayed in a central location
Correct Answer: Use highly visible posters, displayed in a central location
Feedback: Agile projects encourage visibility (transparency). Except when absolutely necessary, nothing should be on a 'need-to-know' basis for these projects. Also called a 'big visible chart', the Agile Alliance states that an information radiator is "the generic term for any of a number of handwritten, drawn, printed or electronic displays which a team places in a highly visible location, so that all team members, as well as passers-by, can see the latest information at a glance: count of automated tests, velocity, incident reports, continuous integration status, and so on." Agile Practice Guide, Project Management Institute Inc., 2017, Page(s) 152

Question Text: You are a project manager of a software development project that is following agile –scrum framework. The product owner and the development team has finalized a clear sprint goal for the upcoming sprint. Who determines how the scrum team will accomplish the goal?
Selected Answer: Product owner.
Correct Answer: The development team.
Feedback: In agile projects, the development teams are self-organized and cross-functional. They are empowered to organize and manage their work. No one tells the development team how to turn product backlog into increments of potentially releasable functionality. The cross-functional team works together to accomplish the sprint goal. Agile Practice Guide - Project Management Institute Inc., 2017, Page(s) – 40-41.

Question Text: During the last sprint of a software development project which is being executed by following scrum framework, a key stakeholder requests a change which may improve the performance of the final product but may also affect the planned schedule. What should the product owner do?
Selected Answer: Analyze the new requirement with the team and check options for refactoring.
Correct Answer: Analyze the new requirement with the team and check options for refactoring.
Feedback: As per the scenario stated in the question, the stakeholder has requested a change (non – functional requirement) which may cause performance improvement. Analyzing the request with the team and identifying options for refactoring is the best choice among all options. Agile Practice Guide - Project Management Institute Inc., 2017, Page(s) – 9, 153.

Question Text: While the team is prioritizing features for the next iteration, they drop some feature from backlog, which features should the agile team drop it?
Selected Answer: Low risk and low value
Correct Answer: High risk and low value
Feedback: The agile team should drop the feature has High-risk and low-value. An ordering of priorities is illustrated follows: 1. High business value, high risk. 2. High business value, low risk. 3. Low business value, low risk. 4. Low business value, high risk.

Question Text: You are project Manager and have been participating in initial discussion with product Managers, business and architect team to reach an agreement on work in progress limit for your team. After analyzing the nature of work and other parameters you have proposed a Work in progress limit of 50 however Business stakeholders want WIP in progress limit to be increased to 75 as there is need to faster time to market. As a Project manager what are the factors you should consider before deciding on WIP limits?
Selected Answer: WIP limits are mostly influenced by Queue size and needs to be determined during the course of the project as more information is available to team
Correct Answer: WIP limits is influenced by Queue and buffer size , both of these needs to be empirically adjusted as required as the project progresses
Feedback: WIP limit is influenced by Queue and buffer size, however it is not recommended to arrive at an accurate WIP and potentially delay the rollout of the project, recommended approach is to empirically adjust through observations.

Question Text: During Sprint Review, customer wants some enhancements to a feature that was completed during the Sprint and was accepted by the Product Owner. How should the team deal with such changes?
Selected Answer: Mark the current story as 'Done' and create a new story for new enhancements.
Correct Answer: Mark the current story as 'Done' and create a new story for new enhancements.
Feedback: Since these changes are enhancements, not defects, the current story should be marked as done. The requested enhancements must go into product backlog as new stories, to be prioritized, estimated and scheduled in due course of time.

Question Text: The Scrum Master has been a technical architect in his previous role. During a Sprint Planning session, he notices team is opting for a solution approach that he feels has a high risk of failure. What should the Scrum Master do?
Selected Answer: Share his apprehensions with the team and let them take the final decision.
Correct Answer: Share his apprehensions with the team and let them take the final decision.
Feedback: Transparency and collective decision making are key characteristics of Agile methods.

Question Text: You are working as a product owner and part of the project that is assigned to you now is to get a piece of the project from a vendor. One of the vendors invites you for a special dinner to discuss this area of the project. What should be your reply to this invitation?
Selected Answer: Politely reject the invitation and request the vendor to send an official proposal
Correct Answer: Politely reject the invitation and request the vendor to send an official proposal
Feedback: As per code of ethics, you should Politely reject the invitation and request the vendor to send an official proposal. As he is one of many vendors then all should be treated equally and wait for all proposals to study them.

Question Text: When is a user story (or feature) usually estimated by a Scrum team?
Selected Answer: A user story is estimated right after its elaboration, close to execution in a Sprint.
Correct Answer: A user story is estimated right after its elaboration, close to execution in a Sprint.
Feedback: Scrum uses the idea of progressive elaboration where a user story is elaborated and estimated just in time – close to execution.

Question Text: A development team continuously showing predictable velocity trends when estimating user stories of size 1, 2, or 3 points but does not have a good track record with stories sized at 5 points and above. What could be the reason behind this special bad track record?
Selected Answer: User Stories are not self-contained and creating misunderstanding
Correct Answer: The team is working on epics not user stories
Feedback: Epics are made up of multiple stories. If the estimation is above a certain threshold these needs to be further break down before it's added to a sprint. Bigger the work, more uncertainties are there as requirements becomes abstract.

Question Text: Oreste is managing a project release using the Scrum model and has decided to colocate the team for the duration of the project. What benefits will Oreste realize by using this approach? (Select three.)
Selected Answer: Increase the effectiveness of team dynamics. Create a continuous learning environment at a reduced cost. Increase knowledge sharing
Correct Answer: Increase the effectiveness of team dynamics. Create a continuous learning environment at a reduced cost. Increase knowledge sharing
Feedback: According to the Agile Practice Guide, colocation improves communication,increases knowledge sharing, enables team member commitment to each other and the project, and creates a low-cost continuous learning environment.

Question Text: A development team is closely working with the customer to design wireframes for each story. The every feature is going in development after the agreement of the client using these wireframes. Initial iterations went well, but in fifth iteration client simply rejected the work by saying this is not what I wanted to. What could be the reason behind the situation?
Selected Answer: Wireframes just provides the starting point for developers to create the system
Correct Answer: Wireframes may not necessarily always convey the working needs
Feedback: Yes, wireframes help to visualize how the next iteration features will look like but it is not everything as it is not working prototype. The development team is required to collaborate not only for UI but also for the intended needs behind user stories. You cannot understand all the needs just by documentation/wireframes; you need to know the actual requirements behind the iteration goal. Now it is also possible that customer has identified wrong customer needs, but the question is not indicating anything about it. Without explicit mention, we cannot assume it. Also, wireframes are just the starting point. However, the best reason is that team could not understand the working needs. If the system is simple, then wireframes can be only one form of documentation. In Agile we focus more on working software rather on documentation.

Question Text: What is the BEST way to estimate the cost of a project?
Selected Answer: Create breakdown of product backlog items into tasks and get time and cost estimate from team members
Correct Answer: Estimate project in story points and determine average velocity.
Feedback: Project size and average velocity give a good idea of the overall cost of a project , option C looks attractive but in agile we do not recommend to do this much advance and detail planning and we expect changes in project scope.

Question Text: The team is struggling to reach a consensus on the estimate for a story that involves a new technology the team is not much familiar with. What should the team do?
Selected Answer: Since the team has low expertise in the required technology, it should use a pessimistic approach and pick the highest individual estimate.
Correct Answer: Team should defer estimating the story and should first run a research spike to explore how this feature could be developed.
Feedback: The high variation in individual estimate due to uncertainty in required technical approach indicates a risk. Running a short time-boxed research spike to gain more knowledge about possible approach is a good way to handle such risks.

Question Text: Team who has recently started implementing KANBAN needs some advice from Agile coach on how to conduct daily standup meetings. If you are an Agile coach what would you recommend?
Selected Answer: Daily standup meetings in KANBAN should always be like that of Scrum where every participants get chance to speak on 3 questions, what did you achieve yesterday, what did you do today and what is stopping your work
Correct Answer: Daily standup meetings in Kanban should focus on flow of work and there should not be limit on how many should participate
Feedback: In Kanban going around asking 3 questions to all like in Sprint is not needed as Board explains the status as well impediments, The focus in standup is flow of work, and there is no limit on participants as kanban is usually for a larger team.

Question Text: It is the Sprint Planning meeting for 3rd sprint of an 8-sprint release. One user story is too large and team decides to split it into smaller stories. There are several ways team could split user stories EXCEPT:
Selected Answer: Splitting the user stories based on the data that will be supported or based on data variations
Correct Answer: Splitting user stories based on relative weightage of risk and business value for each of the smaller stories.
Feedback: Relative weightage of risk and business value is used to prioritize user stories, but is not recommended to split a user story into smaller stories.

Question Text: A team member has been coming late to the Daily scrum despite repeated reminders from Scrum Master. How could the Scrum Master attempt to correct this behaviour?
Selected Answer: Enforce the late arrival penalty (monetary contribution to team fund) that the team agreed upon.
Correct Answer: Enforce the late arrival penalty (monetary contribution to team fund) that the team agreed upon.
Feedback: If the team has already agreed upon a penalty for late arrival, it must be enforced without delay. It could be an item for retrospective only if the penalty fails to correct this behaviour.

Question Text: A team usually follows a 3-month release cycle with several 2-week sprints, but the customer is too busy to attend Sprint-end product reviews. He insists on release-end demo only. Do you anticipate a problem here?
Selected Answer: Lack of timely customer feedback may result in big changes later on
Correct Answer: Lack of timely customer feedback may result in big changes later on
Feedback: Timely customer feedback is essential to confirm if the team efforts are headed in the right direction. Delays in feedback are bound to cause rework at a later stage, often with bigger batch sizes.

Question Text: As an Agile Practitioner how could you ensure stakeholder vision and objectives are shared by the team?
Selected Answer: Arrange for a meeting where stakeholders share their vision and objectives with the development team.
Correct Answer: Ensure that stakeholders interact with developers on a regular basis.
Feedback: Regular interaction between customer and development team – for requirement elicitation, customer tests and product demos – is of utmost importance to ensure team understands and shares stakeholder vision and objectives.

Question Text: While most developers design and code their stories, you have an experienced architect in the team who is primarily responsible for code review of other team members to ensure consistency and quality in design. But the practice of doing code review (and possible rework) after development is complete on a story is creating friction among team members, often resulting in low morale. As an Agile Practitioner, how you may address this issue:
Selected Answer: Discuss with team the possibility of adopting new technical practices to ensure early design and code review, thereby reducing waste on rework.
Correct Answer: Discuss with team the possibility of adopting new technical practices to ensure early design and code review, thereby reducing waste on rework.
Feedback: Agile methods lay great emphasis on continuous improvement, and if something is not working, team must try to find better way of doing things. And, by default, most such decisions must be taken with team consensus.

Question Text: The customer tells you in the middle of the release that one feature that is already in progress is no longer required. This feature is an epic and significant effort has already gone into the development. What should the team do next?
Selected Answer: Stop development on this feature right away and read just the release milestones.
Correct Answer: Stop development on this feature right away and read just the release milestones.
Feedback: Responding to change is one of the key characteristics of Agile project management. If the customer does not want something anymore, it must not be built. The team should now work with customer to understand the changed business priorities and read just release milestones.

Question Text: An established team of 8 members is known for higher performance and low defect rates. They usually pick 20-25 stories for execution during their 30-day sprint. As an Agile Practitioner, what do you think the team could try to step up their agility?
Selected Answer: Reduce sprint duration to limit increment size and increase review frequency.
Correct Answer: Reduce sprint duration to limit increment size and increase review frequency.
Feedback: Since there is significant number of stories in each Sprint, the team could try 2- or 3-week sprints with less number of stories. It will improve review frequency with the customer, in turn reducing the amount of rework.

Question Text: The velocity of a team went down because Product Owner did not provide requirement clarification to the team. What should the Scrum Master do?
Selected Answer: Take the responsibility of getting requirement clarifications from the Product Owner next sprint onwards
Correct Answer: Tell the team it is their responsibility to obtain requirement clarification from the Product Owner
Feedback: Scrum Master's role is to facilitate a team be self-organized in their work. In that direction, he should encourage team to get requirement details from PO on its own.

Question Text: When should you freeze acceptance criteria for a user story?
Selected Answer: Never – the acceptance criteria for a user story must stay open for discussion and negotiation even during Sprint.
Correct Answer: Never – the acceptance criteria for a user story must stay open for discussion and negotiation even during Sprint.
Feedback: Refer Agile principle – "Welcome changing requirements, even late in development. Agile processes harness change for the customer's competitive advantage." In adaptive life cycle requirements are emerged instead of baselined.

Question Text: Does estimation differ for product backlog (PB) items and the sprint backlog (SB) items?
Selected Answer: PB items are estimated in days and SB items are estimated in ideal hours
Correct Answer: PB items are estimated in story points and SB items are estimated in ideal hours
Feedback: Story points are a unit of measure for expressing the overall size of a user story, feature, or other piece of work. When we estimate with story points, we assign a point value to each item. When we estimate the number of ideal days that a user story will take to develop, test, and accept.

Question Text: What would be your most important recommendation to the management who are procuring new office space and there is a plan to transition from traditional project management to agile?
Selected Answer: Co-locate employees working on the same project
Correct Answer: Co-locate employees working on the same project
Feedback: For agile projects, co-location of team members is the most important consideration, wherever possible.

Question Text: Which of the following statements is true? (Select two.)
Selected Answer: A team that uses an Agile approach is more likely to produce greater business value.
Correct Answer: The goal of project management is to produce business value in the best way possible. An organization should choose the delivery method that best produces business value.
Feedback: According to the Agile Practice Guide, the goal of project management is to produce business value. The method that a team uses to deliver value should be based on which would yield the most successful outcome. This is often driven by the nature of the project and the circumstances surrounding the project.

Question Text: An agile project is running its fifth iteration out of ten. After the last iteration review, the team members receive feedback from the security department about regulation with which the project must comply. Which two actions should the project manager take? (choose two)
Selected Answer: Ask the team members to analyze the impact of including this regulation
Correct Answer: Ask the product owner to include the requirement in the product backlog. Ask the security department for details about regulations
Feedback: As mentioned in the question ( The project MUST comply with these regulations.) 1- Ask the product owner to include the requirements in the product backlog. 2- . Ask the security department for details about regulations.

Question Text: How will the selection of a predictive project life cycle shape the way the project is carried out? (Choose three)
Selected Answer: A single final product will be delivered at the end of the project. The requirements will be determined upfront before the project execution begins. Changes will be constrained to the extent possible
Correct Answer: A single final product will be delivered at the end of the project. The requirements will be determined upfront before the project execution begins. Changes will be constrained to the extent possible
Feedback: With a traditional waterfall project, the project requirements and scope are typically determined during initial project planning. Once the project management plan is approved, changes are constrained through a robust change management process. The product or result of the project is then typically delivered in its final form at the end of the project. The incorrect answer choices are indicative of agile project management methodologies.

Question Text: A recent internal survey indicated that most employees are apprehensive about transition from waterfall to Scrum, suggesting the organization may not be ready for Agile adoption just yet. As an Agile Practitioner responsible for managing one team, what is your best option?
Selected Answer: Start introducing some of the Agile practices within your team while still using traditional project management at the higher level.
Correct Answer: Start introducing some of the Agile practices within your team while still using traditional project management at the higher level.
Feedback: Scrum is a big bang approach and may sometimes receive resistance from team members. A team can still adopt agility and benefit from it by taking a piecemeal approach.

Question Text: Which of the following is addressed within the resource management plan? (Select three.)
Selected Answer: Recognition and rewards. Compliance. Safety
Correct Answer: Recognition and rewards. Compliance. Safety
Feedback: The resource management plan describes when and how resource requirements will be met. It addresses things such as staff acquisition, timetable of when the team will be acquired, release criteria, training needs, recognition and rewards, compliance, and safety. It doesn't, however, define the roles and responsibilities, which is a separate output of the human resource management planning process.

Question Text: Which of the following reflect principles listed in the Agile Manifesto? (Select three.)
Selected Answer: The best architectures, requirements, and designs emerge from teams that are directed by strong leaders.
Correct Answer: Working software is the primary measure of progress. Our highest priority is to satisfy the customer through early and continuous delivery of valuable software. Simplicity—the art of maximizing the amount of work not done—is essential.
Feedback: Working software is the primary measure of progress. Our highest priority is to satisfy the customer through early and continuous delivery of valuable software. Simplicity—the art of maximizing the amount of work not done—is essential.

Question Text: When does a Scrum team create and elaborate user stories in detail?
Selected Answer: User stories may be created early but must be elaborated close to execution in a Sprint.
Correct Answer: User stories may be created early but must be elaborated close to execution in a Sprint.
Feedback: Just like other Agile methods, Scrum uses the idea of progressive elaboration where requirement details are listed out just in time – close to execution.

Question Text: Sue is the leader of an enterprise PMO. Recently, she rolled out a quarterly project auditing process. Each quarter, 10 percent of the project portfolio would be randomly audited. What is the leading motivator and benefit of project audits? (Select two.)
Selected Answer: Identifying key legal and/or contractual requirements
Correct Answer: Determining potential threats to compliance. Monitoring compliance against published standards and policies
Feedback: PMOs may facilitate project audits as a means of monitoring compliance against published standards, policies, and procedures published by the PMO and/or the company. A key benefit of project audits is that they serve as a tool for identifying potential threats to compliance, such as legal or contractual requirements.

Question Text: Which of the following best describe characteristics of a product backlog? (Select three.)
Selected Answer: It is prioritized by a business representative. Work is pulled from the top of the backlog. It contains a list of prioritized work.
Correct Answer: It is prioritized by a business representative. Work is pulled from the top of the backlog. It contains a list of prioritized work.
Feedback: A backlog contains a prioritized list of all work encapsulated in a project. It is used to track, review, and regulate work. The team generally pulls work from the top of the backlog, and the backlog is continuously refined over the course of the project. The product owner is responsible for maintaining the backlog and is a representative of the business.

Question Text: A scrum team has completed its first iteration for an important project. A burndown chart indicates that the project is behind schedule. Which two actions should the project manager take to manage impediments and improve the team's velocity?
Selected Answer: Look for processes that cause bottlenecks and slow down the team's agility. Work with the team to remove impediments as quickly as possible.
Correct Answer: Look for processes that cause bottlenecks and slow down the team's agility. Work with the team to remove impediments as quickly as possible.
Feedback: 1- Work with the team to remove impediments as quickly as possible. 2- Look for processes that cause bottlenecks and slow down the team's agility.

Question Text: You are a project manager working as a consultant for a company that is in startup mode. One of your responsibilities for this week is to create an organizational chart. What format can you use to display an organizational chart? (Select three.)
Selected Answer: Hierarchical type. Matrix-based. Text-oriented
Correct Answer: Hierarchical type. Matrix-based. Text-oriented
Feedback: A run chart is a type of quality tool and therefore not a format you would use to display an organizational chart.

Question Text: It is day 7 of a 10-day (2-week) sprint and as developers are finishing development tasks, the testing tasks are piling up. There is a risk all stories may not get done within Sprint timelines. As a Scrum Master of a high-performing crossfunctional team, how you may best address this issue:
Selected Answer: Urge developers to pick up testing tasks to share the testing load, wherever possible.
Correct Answer: Urge developers to pick up testing tasks to share the testing load, wherever possible.
Feedback: Finishing the story in a Scrum team is everyone's responsibility, even if it means developers pick up testing tasks or the other way around. There are no clearly defined roles within Development Team precisely for the same reason. Every member must be committed to meet team's Sprint goal whatever it takes.

Question Text: The benefits of maintaining and making visible a prioritized list of threats and issues facing the team include the following EXCEPT:
Selected Answer: Elevate accountability
Correct Answer: Find root cause of the problem
Feedback: The primary purpose creating an impediments list and making it visible is to expedite effective resolution, not to find the root cause of the problem.

Question Text: Which of the following approaches to agility lays great emphasis on eliminating waste:
Selected Answer: Lean
Correct Answer: Lean
Feedback: 'Eliminate Waste' is one of the seven key principles of Lean.

Question Text: Why does an Agile team need to elicit and prioritize important non-functional requirements (such as security and performance) early on?
Selected Answer: To minimize the probability of failure
Correct Answer: To minimize the probability of failure
Feedback: If not dealt in a timely manner, issues like security and performance may require big design changes later, often failing the project. Please note that we are only talking about understanding and prioritizing non-functional requirements here – this does not mean that we need to work on all non-functional requirements at the beginning of the project.

Question Text: Which of the following practice will best support the transfer of knowledge to benefit future project? (Choose three) multiple-choice
Selected Answer: Ensure that the lessons learned register is listed as a configuration element in the configuration management plan
Correct Answer: Conduct regular retrospective meeting with the project team and relevant stakeholders. Document knowledge gained in the lessons learned register throughout the project. Ensure that the lessons learned register is finalized and transferred to the lessons learned repository
Feedback: Answering this question correctly requires an understanding of how knowledge gained throughout the project should be tracked and recorded. The lessons learned register should be revised throughout the course of the project, anytime information that might be helpful later in the current project or applicable to future projects is gained. Additionally, periodic lesson learned meetings (retrospectives) might be held specifically to aid in the recognition and documenting of knowledge gained. During project closure, the lessons learned register is finalized and transferred to an organizational process set (OPA) referred to as the lessons learned repository. The lessons learned repository can then serve as an input for future projects to improve performance.

Question Text: A junior developer took 12 hours to complete a relatively complex task that was estimated by the team as a 4-hour task. How should an agile team handle such a case?
Selected Answer: Assign a mentor for this developer for next few sprints.
Correct Answer: Let team members estimate their own tasks.
Feedback: Task assignment and estimation should be pull-based – members must self-volunteer for tasks and give their own estimates. In this case the issue is taking more time than estimate; it is not about lacking the ability to complete the task.

Question Text: Average velocity of a team over past several sprints has been 30 story points. In the current Sprint, two stories got stuck due to external dependencies and ended up bringing down team velocity to 20 story points. How many story points should the team pick for execution in the upcoming sprint?
Selected Answer: Go with whatever number the team feels comfortable with
Correct Answer: Go with whatever number the team feels comfortable with
Feedback: The historical velocity is only a 'guideline' for future sprint planning. In the end, the development team decides exactly how many points should be picked up for the next Sprint, based on their confidence level.

Question Text: In an effort to facilitate close communication with external stakeholders, management has decided to co-locate a subject matter expert from customer side with the team. The team however is resistant to the idea - they fear it will create unnecessary work pressure and may expose the team's internal issues and weaknesses to the customer. As an Agile Practitioner, what would you consider your best first move?
Selected Answer: Side with the team and vote against the idea.
Correct Answer: Call a team meeting where you explain the value of customer collaboration for building good quality products and discuss the validity of their fears.
Feedback: While Agile teams see a clear value in customer co-location, if a team is resistant to the idea, the first step should be to discuss the validity of their apprehensions.

Question Text: Why do Agile methods recommend frequent reviews of work products via code reviews, testing and product reviews?
Selected Answer: It helps incorporate improvements into the overall process and product.
